cards.text: It's the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, king of Persia (Ezra 4:24). God's people are back at work on the LORD's temple (Haggai 1:14). And the word of the LORD comes to Haggai the prophet once again.
This time the LORD of Hosts opens with a question, and Haggai has to go get an official ruling on it. Not a guess, not a hunch, a RULING.

cards.question: Who does the LORD of Hosts tell Haggai to ask for a ruling?

cards.text: Here's the question, and it's a good one. A man carries consecrated meat in the fold of his garment, and it touches bread, stew, wine, oil or any other food.

cards.question: Consecrated meat in a man's garment touches other food. True or false: the priests rule that the food becomes holy.

cards.text: So holy doesn't rub off on the food. Then Haggai flips the question and asks about someone defiled by contact with a corpse.

cards.question: If someone defiled by contact with a corpse touches that food, the priests rule that it becomes ___.

cards.text: Then Haggai brings it home, speaking for the LORD: "So it is with this people and this nation before Me". Holy doesn't rub off but defiled does, which is me with dough in my mustache, because ONE swipe and the whole bakery is covered.

cards.question: True or false: the LORD says whatever this people offers there is holy.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells them to "consider carefully from this day forward" and has them look back.

cards.question: The LORD has the people think back on His temple. Back to a time before what?

answers.text: Before one stone sat on another
Before its gold was carried off

cards.question: Back then, the harvest came up short. Someone came expecting a heap of twenty ephahs of grain and found only ___.

cards.text: Same story at the winepress: they came to draw out fifty baths and got twenty. That's like opening a box marked two dozen cookies and finding twelve, and friend, I would be writing a LETTER.

cards.question: The LORD says He struck all the work of their hands with blight, mildew and hail. What does He say the people did?

answers.text: They did not turn to Him

cards.text: Blight, mildew, hail. That's three alarms, and they hit snooze on all three.
Then comes that line again, "consider carefully from this day forward," and this time God names the day: the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month.

cards.question: God names the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the same day this message came to Haggai. What happened on that day?

answers.text: The foundation of the LORD's temple was laid
The LORD's temple was finished at last
The ark was brought into the temple

cards.text: Then the LORD asks them a question of His own: "Is there still seed in the barn?"

cards.question: True or false: the vine, the fig, the pomegranate and the olive tree have already yielded fruit.
The trees haven't yielded fruit yet. But from this day on, God says He will ___ them.

findings.problem: The fill-in-the-blank asks for the exact grain count (ten vs fifteen vs five). The setup only says 'the harvest came up short,' so any smaller number fits. Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason toward ten, so getting it right is luck. A better question would ask about the shortfall itself, such as how much less they got.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats Haggai 2:17 (blight, mildew, hail, and the people not turning), which card 14 already covered and answered. It adds nothing new from the passage and is a joke recap. The snooze joke should ride on a card that moves the passage forward, such as card 14's setup or card 16.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: 'A question of His own' suggests the earlier question was not the LORD's. In Haggai 2:11-12, the question about consecrated meat is inside the LORD of Hosts' own words. Card 2 itself says 'the LORD of Hosts opens with a question.' Card 18's framing contradicts both the text and card 2.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The question reads 'The trees haven't yielded fruit yet. But from this day on, God says He will ___ them.' Here 'them' grammatically points to the trees. In Haggai 2:19 the LORD says 'I will bless you,' meaning the people. As written, the question misstates who is blessed.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.
